notes: 2026-08-19 review of 13 commits (606ad45..79f896b, oldest to newest) on branch upstream-review/2026-08-19-sync-hardening. Full backend gate (.venv/bin/pytest -q) passing at 303 tests; no frontend files were touched by this pass.

606ad45 (n-way reconciliation safety hardening): manual port, done. Two-pass removal confirmation, ISRC/catalog-name normalization, identity-rebinding history, fail-closed provider pagination. Merged against this project's state_key multi-account namespacing.

f787d0d (classify changes + keyless Spotify): manual port, partial. Ported the reconcile() change-diagnostics/log_protected/log_repair instrumentation and the key2isrc peer-order-independence fix (both additive, low risk). Did NOT port 'keyless Spotify' (spotify_cookie.py becoming a full peer with no developer app) -- it overlaps heavily with this project's existing per-account cookie architecture and needs a human product decision; classified blocked. Did NOT port the frontend activity-feed classification UI (LiveFeed.tsx, NeedsALook.tsx, FilterSelect.tsx, etc.) -- cosmetic and heavily diverged locally; deferred, not required for the backend fields to be safe.
b2e2c55 and 09b4794 (activity filter label/stability fixes): not applicable. Both are follow-on fixes to the frontend classification UI that f787d0d introduced and this project did not port.

9e315e1 (remote Spotify OAuth callbacks): manual port, partial. Ported SONGMIRROR_PUBLIC_URL support in web/routers/accounts.py._redirect_uri for Docker/reverse-proxy deployments. Did NOT port the SpotifyConnector SPOTIFY_AUTH_MODE oauth/cookie toggle -- this project's Connector._get() already does a store-then-env fallback for the default account and deliberately never falls back to env for a named account (multi-account credential isolation); re-adding upstream's toggle would be redundant and could weaken that isolation. Classified not applicable.
ba30fbf (isolate archive connections per provider, one-way sync): manual port, done. Each one-way worker thread now gets its own sqlite3 connection instead of sharing one across threads.

d2c14bb (render cached data before revalidation): blocked. Introduces a new frontend runtime dependency (swr, plus dequal/use-sync-external-store transitively). Per project-contract.md, dependency/lockfile changes need a fresh security audit and the full test/build gate; this needs a human decision on accepting the new dependency (and network access to properly vet/install/audit it) before it's ported. Not attempted.

5b08253 (harden Qobuz and Apple playlist reads): manual port, done. Apple session-rebuild-and-fail-closed after repeated 5xx; services/playlists.py._pl_id() now always returns a string (Qobuz emits numeric ids).

694144e (preserve ordering and hydrate Spotify counts): manual port, done. Cross-provider added_at normalization (ISO/unix-s/unix-ms) replacing a naive lexicographic sort, used by one-way compute_diff, N-way reconcile's ADD-phase sort, and transfers.py. Amazon/Deezer/YTMusic additions now go one API call per track (a provider can stamp/reorder a whole batch). hydrate_playlist_counts() browse hook for cookie-mode Spotify, adapted to key its count cache by (account_id, playlist_id).

107c463 (enforce Spotify authority and harden playlist browsing): manual port, partial. This is a much larger commit than its title suggests. Ported: matching.py creative-version-marker guard (rejects a live/acoustic/remix/etc. match against the studio original in fuzzy search, one-way and N-way); archive.reset_playlist_peer_state() wired into both run_target() and _run_nway() so a recreated playlist bootstraps from the current source instead of reading its predecessor's baseline as a collapsed read; a real bug fix where run_target()'s per-target aggregate dict dropped the 'deferred' count. NOT ported: the TargetTransientError rate-limit/server-error retry-and-defer mechanism for mirror_pair()/reconcile(), plus cross-provider identity-crosswalk and archived-recording-match reuse when resolving tracks for a recreated destination playlist -- a substantial rewrite of the one-way resolve/write path that deserves its own dedicated, unhurried review given how central it is to sync correctness. Also not ported: the playlist_cache/playlist_track_cache tables and the full playlist-inspector UI feature (external links, cover art, pagination, bulk delete) -- large, UI-heavy, and grouped with the d2c14bb dependency-blocking decision since it depends on similar not-yet-accepted frontend patterns.
535e880 (preserve YouTube newest-first playlist sorting): not applicable. Fixes a bug inside PlaylistDetailModal.tsx, which is part of the 107c463 playlist-inspector feature that was not ported.

ba092ff (add authoritative provider groups): blocked. A substantial new sync mode (a subset of providers as trusted 'authorities' contributing membership changes, others as pure mirrors) touching archive.py, config.py, runner.py, targets/base.py, services/syncs.py, services/sync_service.py, web/routers/syncs.py, and a new sync-wizard UI step. This is a new feature (not a bug fix), very large (1090+ insertions across 23 files), and interacts deeply with the n-way reconciliation safety semantics already carefully ported from 606ad45/694144e/107c463. Needs its own dedicated review pass rather than being rushed alongside 12 other commits; not attempted.

79f896b (isolate mirror read failures): blocked. Entirely a follow-on fix to ba092ff's authoritative-groups model (uses the authority_sources parameter and _run_authoritative_group, neither of which exist locally) -- cannot be ported independently of ba092ff. Note for a future pass: this commit also adds archive.get_snapshots() + a TIDAL playlist_tracks() fallback that reuses last-known archived metadata for a delisted catalog entry instead of failing the whole read closed; that specific piece is architecturally separable from the authority-groups isolation logic and could be cherry-picked on its own if useful before ba092ff is tackled.

Protected-surface impact: none of the ported commits touched data/sync_music.db semantics, Musify/Sonora import/pause behavior, playlist recovery-version guards, or Sonora pairing/LAN-only web-UI security. songmirror/web/routers/accounts.py (a protected path) was touched only for the additive SONGMIRROR_PUBLIC_URL redirect-URI feature; reviewed carefully, tests added.
